_comment: The optional Ice and Fire compatibility of Spider Queen: Hungry Craft (Necromancy IV prototype 2).
It is a configuration of its own, and every one of its properties says the same thing: a game without Ice and
Fire must not be touched by it at all.
required  : false - a mixin of this configuration that can not be applied is a logged note, never a crash.
client    : everything in here only changes which texture a dragon is drawn with, and whether Ice and Fire's
eye layer draws on a woken dragon, so a dedicated server never loads these classes at all.
plugin    : the gate. It answers 'shouldApplyMixin' with no while Ice and Fire is not installed, and a mixin
that is not applied is a mixin whose class Mixin never loads - which is what keeps the names of
another mod out of a game that does not have it.
mixins    : the hooks that both the server and the client need. EntityDragonBaseRiderMixin answers the one
question the riding of Ice and Fire hangs on (Entity#getControllingPassenger) for a skeleton under
a contract, and it has to be there on both sides: the entity asks it while it moves on the server
and while it is drawn on the client.
refmap    : the reference map of the rider hook, and the only entry it has is named after a VANILLA method
(Entity#getControllingPassenger) that Ice and Fire merely overrides. The generated refmap of the
main configuration can not carry that name - the Minecraft mappings do not know the class of
another mod - so the one entry is written into spiderqueen_hungrycraft_iaf.refmap.json by hand. The
two client hooks need no entry at all: they are remap = false and name methods of Ice and Fire
itself, whose names are identical in a development workspace and in a published jar.
